card.summary: The TAKE IT DOWN Act makes it a federal crime to publish or threaten to publish nonconsensual intimate visual depictions, including both authentic photos/videos and computer-generated digital forgeries (deepfakes) of adults and minors. It also requires public internet platforms that host user-generated content to create a clear process for individuals to request the removal of such images and to take them down within 48 hours of receiving a valid request.

summary: H.R. 633, known as the TAKE IT DOWN Act, prohibits the nonconsensual online publication of intimate visual depictions of individuals, covering both authentic images and computer-generated digital forgeries. It requires covered online platforms to establish formal notice-and-removal processes and to remove reported content within 48 hours. Violators face criminal penalties, including fines and imprisonment, alongside mandatory restitution and forfeiture, while platforms that comply in good faith are protected from liability.

affected_groups.effect: Gain the right to request swift removal of such content from online platforms and can seek criminal prosecution, restitution, and forfeiture against individuals who publish or threaten to publish these depictions.
affected_groups.group: Adults depicted in nonconsensual intimate images or digital forgeries

affected_groups.effect: Receive protections via criminal prohibitions against publication meant to harass, abuse, or gratify sexual desire, along with platform removal mechanisms and heightened criminal penalties for offenders.
affected_groups.group: Minors subjected to nonconsensual intimate images or digital forgeries

affected_groups.effect: Must create a visible notice and removal system, remove reported nonconsensual intimate depictions within 48 hours, make reasonable efforts to delete identical copies, and face FTC enforcement for noncompliance while receiving liability protection for good-faith takedowns.
Subject to federal criminal penalties, including fines and prison sentences of up to 3 years depending on the victim's age and whether the depiction is authentic or a digital forgery.
affected_groups.group: Individuals who publish or threaten to publish nonconsensual intimate images

key_provisions: Prohibits the knowing online publication of nonconsensual intimate visual depictions of adults where publication is intended to cause or causes harm, and where the subject had a reasonable expectation of privacy.
Prohibits the knowing online publication of intimate visual depictions of minors with intent to abuse, humiliate, harass, degrade, or sexually gratify any person.
Bans the publication of computer-generated digital forgeries of both adults and minors under similar conditions of nonconsent and harmful intent.
Imposes criminal penalties, mandatory restitution, and property forfeiture for individuals convicted of publishing or threatening to publish prohibited intimate depictions.
Mandates that covered platforms establish an accessible notice-and-removal process for victims to request the deletion of nonconsensual intimate visual depictions.
Requires covered platforms to remove reported depictions and known identical copies within 48 hours of receiving a valid request.
Empowers the Federal Trade Commission to enforce platform compliance as an unfair or deceptive act or practice.

summary_detail.significance: The bill creates a nationwide federal standard criminalizing the nonconsensual distribution of intimate media and deepfakes while imposing strict 48-hour removal timelines on interactive internet platforms under Federal Trade Commission oversight.
